answer: Each voucher owns one orchard row and plants identity trees in it, the nth tree costing $10 times n squared in collateral. Each vouch dyes its tree with the voucher's pigment, so a proven fake traces the stain back to its voucher. Seven juniper auditors walk the rows weekly; one fraud proof burns the voucher's whole stack and voids every tree in its row. 100 clones in one row cost $10 times the sum of 1 squared through 100 squared, $3,383,500, while 100 honest agents planting one tree each pay $1,000. A forger buying a whole orchard to hide one bad apple pays for every tree in it.
